stories.title: The Emerald Room
stories.alt: Illustrative forest-green room with warm brass details
stories.intro: Deep green, soft daylight and a quiet sense of belonging.
stories.heading: Let the colour set the pace.
paragraphs: A green kitchen can feel cocooning without feeling closed in. Balance the deeper cabinet tone with a lighter wall and keep the largest surfaces calm, so the room has space to breathe.

Before choosing a finish, look at samples in your own room at different times of day. Warm metal details and natural textures can soften the palette; a limited selection keeps the overall composition clear.

stories.title: The Walnut Room
stories.alt: Illustrative walnut kitchen with a warm natural palette
stories.intro: Wood grain, long lines and the warmth of an unhurried morning.
stories.heading: Give natural texture room to speak.
paragraphs: Use the direction of wood grain to guide the eye. A continuous horizontal line can make a compact arrangement feel more settled, while taller panels can emphasise the height of a room.
Pair a strong wood texture with quieter surfaces. Collect samples together before deciding: the relationship between the wood tone, floor and worktop matters more than any single finish.

stories.title: The Ivory Room
stories.alt: Illustrative ivory room with soft daylight and framed cabinetry
stories.intro: A softer neutral, framed doors and light that moves through the day.
stories.heading: Build a neutral palette with depth.
paragraphs: Ivory is a family of tones rather than a single colour. Put warm and cool samples next to your wall and floor finishes to see which combinations feel coherent in your actual light.
Framed doors introduce rhythm without a busy palette. Let shadow, texture and a small number of contrasting details provide the variation, rather than adding more colours.

stories.title: Marble at Dusk
stories.alt: Illustrative dark stone island in an atmospheric kitchen
stories.intro: A sculptural centrepiece, quiet stone and the changing evening light.
stories.heading: Choose where the room makes its statement.
paragraphs: An island can act as the visual anchor of a kitchen. If its surface has pronounced veining, simplify the surrounding materials so that the pattern remains intentional.

Sketch the routes around the island before settling on its shape. Think about open appliance doors, places to pause and how a second person moves through the same space. A planner is a starting point; final clearances need a measured design.

stories.title: Water & Warmth
stories.alt: Illustrative sink area with warm metal details and a pale worktop
stories.intro: Making the most-used corner of the kitchen feel considered.
stories.heading: Plan around the everyday.
paragraphs: Start with what happens around the sink: rinsing vegetables, washing pans, setting down a cup. Leave useful surface space nearby and think about where the dishwasher and waste storage belong.

A tap finish can connect the sink area to the rest of the room. Explore it alongside handles and lighting, then confirm the plumbing, care requirements and fitting details with your chosen specification.

stories.title: A Place for Everything
stories.alt: Illustrative organised kitchen storage and cabinet details
stories.intro: An easier room begins with understanding what you reach for.
stories.heading: Design from the inside out.
paragraphs: List the things you use daily before deciding where cupboards go. Keep preparation tools near the work surface and occasional pieces away from the busiest routes.

Drawers, tall storage and corner fittings solve different problems. Consider how you reach, bend and move rather than filling every available space with a mechanism. Confirm fit and load requirements when the cabinetry is specified.
